body.objective: Test whether the selected compensator repair preserves a healthy relational clock and causal redshift observable after its trace/scalar or topological sector is included.
body.stop_condition: Import the A/B comparison verdict, selected action/carrier hashes and the existing healthy Berger clock/redshift certificates. Refuse an ambiguous or NEITHER selection. Derive the clock, emitter, receiver and detector rows from the selected action, including every scalaron or three-form/topological response and antifield completion. Prove the relevant Cartan/charge identity, causal support and gauge invariance of one relational redshift observable; compare it exactly with the pre-repair Berger result. Determine whether the repair preserves the physical phase clock, changes the measured redshift, introduces an observable extra response, or removes the clock. Emit one exact response certificate, independent action-variation/causal replay and atlas fragment.
body.current_gate: relational-clock and redshift survival in the selected changed theory
body.forbid: no observer rows imported from the naive compensator carrier; no coordinate-frequency ratio called redshift; no clock survival inferred from field counting; no raw D substituted for K_Berger; no detector particle, scattering, positivity or phenomenology claim
activates: or a clock/observation obstruction that invalidates the selected repair
body.resource_hint: DOWNSTREAM GATED. This supersedes the stranded naive-compensator observer route once a changed action is selected.
notes: Candidate B fails the programme if the volume constraint removes the physical clock.
Candidate A must include the scalar response even if the observable ultimately projects it out.
